anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-layer statements or transaction design force the engine to process and retain far more data, rows, or time in flight than business logic really requires.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Engine and session memory structures grow beyond the safe capacity of the host, provoking paging, OOM events, cache churn, or instance restarts.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk pages or index structures are physically or logically corrupted, breaking key order, page links, or heap-to-index consistency.

When these three root causes coincide, their symptoms interleave and intensify: oversized scans and long-running transactions inflate buffer-pool residency and per-query work areas, driving sustained memory pressure; this in turn accelerates paging, CPU stalls, and unplanned restarts. Each crash or forced restart increases the likelihood that unsettled dirty pages are left partially written, surfacing new checksum or index-consistency errors. Meanwhile, existing corruption forces the optimizer to abandon selective indexes, converting many requests into full scans that further bloat memory demand and prolong lock holding, thereby amplifying the long-tail latency already introduced by sub-optimal workload logic. Administrators may observe a feedback loop of repeated slow-query log entries, escalating RSS growth, OOM killer or cluster eviction events, intermittent duplicate or missing rows, and sudden plan regressions that are hard to attribute to a single layer.

Causally, inefficient SQL design begins the spiral by overstressing memory. The resulting pressure heightens the chance of engine stalls, spill-to-disk, or crash recovery gaps that can corrupt pages or indexes. Once corruption appears, the engine compensates with full scans and page rereads, inflating memory consumption and extending transaction lifetimes, which in turn perpetuates memory exhaustion. The intertwined effects of logical inefficiencies, memory starvation, and structural corruption thus reinforce each other, degrading performance, stability, and data correctness across both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_description: Columns participating in a foreign key are renamed
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with logical data inconsistency, structural corruption, uniqueness conflicts, or referential-integrity rules being violated by the workload or storage state.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate data consistency, inspect constraints and index integrity, and check whether data-cleaning, repair, or workload correction is required before retrying.
